newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels says he has accepted an assurance from the four major banks that they had not colluded and discussed their decision to reduce their interest rates by an identical amount. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has warned the banks that the government still seeks a very competitive financial sector in Australia. Page 1.

The Finance Sector Union is seeking a seven percent a year pay rise for over 36,000 employees at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia. The bank's management, however, has said it will seek to tie enterprise bargaining to the stripping back of the bank's award and will refuse to guarantee the retaining of all award conditions. Page 3.

The value of Australia's fishing industry has fallen for the first time in over a decade with a slide of two percent to A$396 million in 1995/96. The major reason for the decline was a drop in the value of pearl oysters, the biggest farmed species, by A$22 million. Page 3.

Treasury Secretary Ted Evans has told a parliamentary committee inflationary expectations are too high to maintain the inflation rate between the Reserve Bank's target of two to three percent. Evans also indicated the current weakness of the Australian dollar would boost the growth of the GDP. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello is expected to oppose a plan which delays by five years the government's plans to cut car tariffs to 15 percent. Although this is the most favoured of two proposals developed by Industry Minister John Moore with the support of Prime Minister John Howard, the plan may result in a fight among the government's economic ministers. Page 1.

Leading creationist academic Allen Roberts has been judged by the Federal Court to have used deception when delivering lectures on Noah's Ark, but Roberts has still claimed a victory for free speech. University of Melbourne professor Ian Pilmer has claimed a victory for science, with Justice Sackville's finding that Roberts had made false representations. Page 1.

A Newspoll has found that Australians are divided on whether the federal government should apologise to Aboriginal people for the 'stolen children'. Exactly half of voters believe the government should apologise, with 10 percent of those polled undecided. Page 1.

Health Minister Michael Wooldridge says there have been a "small number of cases" where blood or tissue donations have been received from donors who have later died of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. The fatal and degenerative disease is the main issue in a A$10 million settlement in a government legal case. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Senior Government economic adviser Ted Evans has told a Senate committee the net impact of a tax rebate seeking to boost national savings could actually be a negative result. Evans told the committee there is a risk that the cost to the government could exceed an increase in savings by individuals. Page 1.

The Hong Kong owner of the half-finished East Circular Quay building has promised to reconsider its plans if asked to do so by the New South Wales Government. The developer, Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels, could consider a compromise which would see it transfer apartment from Bennelong Point to a new development. Page 1.

A 33-year-old Melbourne man has been arrested over an extortion threat involving the contamination of Nestle products. The man contacted the company 13 days ago and said packs of yoghurt had been contaminated. Page 1.

The governing council of the University of New South Wales has voted to introduce fees of up to A$100,000 for some undergraduate students next year. Vice-chancellor John Niland had introduced the proposal, which now complements a similar decision made by he University of Sydney. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Education Minister Phil Gude will launch today a new proposal to give Victorian state schools the power to hire teachers, borrow money to expand, and use outside expertise. Gude believes Victoria should change to a "one model fits all" system to provide schools with more independence. Page A1.

Murdoch Institute for Research scientists have identified and cloned the DNA of an "engine" to ensure chromosomes deliver genes capable or removing inherited disorders. The discovery may provide a treatment for single-gene defects such as cystic fibrosis. Page A1.

Federal Court Justice Ronald Sackville has found Sydney church elder Allen Roberts misrepresented the extent of his involvement in a geological search, where Roberts claimed the remnants of Noah's Ark were located. Sackville found Roberts' claims that he had carried out tests on the artefacts were false and misleading. Page A2.

Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley has accused the government of selectively quoting from a Labor Government submission to the High Court that argued against compensation for the stolen generation of Aboriginals. Beazley said Labor had dismissed compensation through the courts on legal advice, but had not dismissed it through the political process. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
